verdict.rationale: dlt is an open-source library that runs wherever Python runs and loads data into destinations the user chooses. Loaded datasets can be read back as records, Pandas frames, or Arrow tables, and users can switch destinations without changing pipeline code, so data is not locked in. However, the evidence never documents a dedicated export-everything or offboarding path, particularly for data, pipelines, and logs held on dltHub managed infrastructure. Missing for 10: a documented full-export/offboarding feature for dltHub-hosted data, explicit open-format export of all workspace data (e.g. Parquet dumps of datasets, schemas, and run history), and independent corroboration of leaving the platform.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: dlt is an open-source Python library that loads data from various, often messy data sources into well-structured datasets.
You can read the result as records, Pandas frames, or Arrow tables.
This approach is especially useful when switching between destinations without modifying the actual pipeline code.
Write the pipeline in Python and run it wherever Python already runs: a laptop, a notebook, Airflow, Dagster, a Lambda, a container.
